name: Matthias
title: Chosen in place of Judas
tagline: Chosen by lot to take Judas's place among the Twelve.
story: The disciple chosen by lot to take the place of Judas Iscariot among the apostles; Scripture names him only on that day.

periods.title: After Scripture
periods.sub: Tradition, by who said it and when

entries.title: With Jesus from John's baptism to the ascension (the condition he met)
Numbered with the eleven
entries.text: He “was numbered with the eleven apostles”.

entries.title: Never named again
entries.text: From then on Acts speaks of Peter “standing up with the eleven” and of “the twelve” (Acts 2:14; 6:2), a number that now includes him, but it never names him again.

entries.title: Clement of Alexandria, Stromata 6.13; quoted by Eusebius, Church History 3.29.4
entries.text: Clement of Alexandria writes that Matthias, “who was not chosen along with them, on showing himself worthy of becoming an apostle, is substituted for Judas”. Eusebius quotes him again for a saying of Matthias, that “we ought to fight against and abuse the flesh”.
entries.who: Clement of Alexandria, Stromata 6.13; quoted by Eusebius, Church History 3.29.4
entries.when: Clement about AD 200; Eusebius about AD 325

entries.title: Eusebius, Church History 1.12.3 and 3.25.6
entries.text: Eusebius reports that Matthias, and the man put forward with him, “are likewise said” to have been among the Seventy (Luke 10:1). He also lists a “Gospel of Matthias” among books put out by heretics under the apostles' names.

entries.title: Acts of Andrew and Matthias (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 8)
entries.text: In the Acts of Andrew and Matthias, the lot sends Matthias to a city of man-eaters, who blind and imprison him until Andrew comes to free him. The translator notes that the Greek texts waver between Matthias and Matthew, and most place the city in Ethiopia.
entries.who: Acts of Andrew and Matthias (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 8)

entries.title: The Contendings of the Apostles (Ethiopic), trans. Budge, pp. 289-294
entries.text: An Ethiopic “Martyrdom of Saint Matthias” has him preach to the men of Damascus and die in peace in a town of Judaea it calls Pelwon (Phalaeon).
entries.who: The Contendings of the Apostles (Ethiopic), trans. Budge, pp. 289-294
entries.when: Ethiopic version about the early 14th century; manuscript 15th century

entries.title: Nicephorus Callistus, as reported by McGiffert
entries.text: Later writers say he preached and was martyred in Ethiopia. Smith (1884) reports it as “it is said”; McGiffert (1890) names the Byzantine historian Nicephorus Callistus for it.
entries.who: Nicephorus Callistus, as reported by McGiffert
entries.when: Byzantine; the earliest source has not been identified here

places.name: Ethiopia
places.note: Tradition: “it is said” (Smith, 1884); the Acts of Andrew and Matthias place the man-eaters' city there. McGiffert (1890) thinks Nicephorus probably meant “Caucasian Ethiopia”, east of the Black Sea.

claim.text: The other man put forward with him.
Peter proposed that the place of Judas be filled.

scripture.text: Scripture does not mention him after Acts 1:26.

items.q: Scripture never names Matthias in the Gospels; Peter's condition implies he had followed Jesus from John's baptism to the ascension (Acts 1:21-22).
Scripture records nothing he said or did after his choice.
Scripture does not say where he went or how he died.

verses.44001012: Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.
verses.44001021: Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
verses.44001022: Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection.
verses.44001023: And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
verses.44001026: And they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.
verses.44002014: ¶ But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:
verses.44006002: Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.
